The man's RIGHT anatomical leg is NEARER the camera and emerges from the shorts opening on the VIEWER-LEFT underneath the near hand and dumbbell.

Lift and advance the NEAR leg from the VIEWER-LEFT shorts opening, tracing the SAME continuous muscular thigh from that near hip to its forward knee and foot. It crosses in front of the far thigh in depth, not across the foot track. The far LEFT leg stays behind on its toes. Cell10=row3,col2: the NEAR RIGHT foot stepping forward, FAR LEFT foot stays planted behind.
Cell11=row3,col3: NEAR RIGHT foot flat ahead and shallow bend; FAR LEFT leg extends back.
Cell12=row3,col4: descend into RIGHT/NEAR-leg forward lunge.

Cell15=row4,col3: push off and bring that NEAR RIGHT foot back toward standing; FAR LEFT foot is the support.
Cell16=row4,col4: standing returned to cell1.
Preserve equal framing/margins and full head, both shoes and both dumbbells inside each square cell. Only change the lower two rows' leg action to the contralateral repetition. Natural muscle definition and proper knee/hip/ankle connections; never duplicate a leg or paste a second knee.
